gallery.filename: USS Alabama (BB-60) fires guns 1943.jpg
gallery.title: File:USS Alabama (BB-60) fires guns 1943.jpg
gallery.artist: Lt. J.A. Hampton, Royal Navy official photographer
gallery.credit: This photograph A 17629 comes from the collections of the Imperial War Museums.
gallery.description: The U.S. Navy battleship USS Alabama (BB-60) firing her 40.6 cm guns during combined British and American fleet exercises. The photograph was taken from the Royal Navy battleship HMS Anson (79).Alabama and USS South Dakota (BB-57) operated with the British Home Fleet in 1943. In June 1943, the ships, together with HMS Duke of York (17) and HMS Anson took part in "Operation Gearbox" (to Spitsbergen).
categories: Black and white photographs of ships
Collections of the Imperial War Museum

gallery.title: File:Forward superstructure of USS Alabama (BB-60), December 1942.jpg
gallery.description: View of the ship's forward superstructure, looking up from the port side during her shakedown period, circa December 1942. Note: Signal flags; Mk.8 fire control radar on Mk.38 main battery gun director (at top); Mk.4 fire control radar on Mk.37 secondary battery gun director at right; radio direction finder "loop" at left.

gallery.filename: Aircraft carriers at Seattle in January 1947.jpg
gallery.title: File:Aircraft carriers at Seattle in January 1947.jpg
gallery.description: U.S. Navy ships at Seattle, Washington (USA), on 9 January 1947. Three aircraft carriers are at Pier 91, USS Bunker Hill (CV-17), USS Bon Homme Richard (CV-31) and USS Essex (CV-9). USS Ticonderoga (CV-14) is at Pier 92. The battleships USS Indiana (BB-58) and USS Alabama (BB-60) are moored opposite of the Ticonderoga.

gallery.artist: U.S. Navy (the image is part of an album of photographs collected by Captain Carlos W. Wieber during his command of the aircraft carrier USS Essex (CV-9) during 1944-1945).
gallery.description: An Imperial Japanese Navy Nakajima B6N ("Jill") releases its torpedo off the starboard bow of the U.S. Navy aircraft carrier USS Essex (CV-9) off Formosa on 14 October 1944. In the background are the battleship USS Alabama (BB-60), right, and a destroyer, center.

gallery.title: File:80-G-K-497 (24915157406).jpg
gallery.artist: National Museum of the U.S. Navy
gallery.description: 80-G-K-497 (Color):  USS Alabama (BB-60).  Closeup view of the left 16"/45 gun of her after turret, with her superstructure beyond.  photographed during her shakedown period, circa December 1942.  note: Ladders on turret faceplate; Mk.8 and Mk.4 fire control radar antennas atop her after gun directors. Official U.S. Navy Photograph, now in the collections of the National Archives.  (2016/02/10)
